hub.title: Local Web UIs
hub.description: Open the web UIs of local devices and sites inside Home Assistant. This entry holds the options for all of them. Devices that link to a local web page (for example ESPHome with web_server) will be offered under Discovered; other sites are added with "Add entry".

web_ui.title: Add a web UI
web_ui.description: Any web page your Home Assistant server can reach: a device, a router, a printer, another server.

data.name: Name
data.trusted_acknowledged: I understand that a trusted web UI gets full administrator control of Home Assistant
data.identity: Tell the site who is viewing

data_description.url: The full address of the page, including http or https and the port if it is not the default.
data_description.mode: Isolated (recommended) keeps the page away from Home Assistant: it cannot read Home Assistant's data or act as you, while its logins and storage still work. Trusted runs it with Home Assistant's own origin, which a few pages need (for example ones using IndexedDB). A trusted page's scripts get full administrator control of Home Assistant, so only use it for pages you fully trust.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn off for devices with self-signed certificates.
data_description.username: Optional. Sent as HTTP Basic or Digest authentication, so you are not asked to log in.
data_description.password: The password for the username. When editing, leave it empty to keep the stored one.
data_description.token_header: For pages that use an API token or key instead of a login: how it is sent with every request. Choose a listed way or type the name of a header. The browser never sees the token.
data_description.token: When editing, leave it empty to keep the stored token. Choose "No token" to remove it.
data_description.identity: Sends the Home Assistant user viewing this web UI to the site with every request, as a short-lived token signed by Home Assistant (an OpenID Connect JWT). The site, or a gateway in front of it such as oauth2-proxy, checks it with the keys Home Assistant publishes; set up the person's details in the Local Web UIs options. Choose a listed way or type the name of a header to send the token in. Send it only to sites you trust: it says who you are.
data_description.audience: The token's audience (aud), which the site checks. Leave empty for the site's own address (scheme, host and port).
data_description.users: Admins can open every web UI. The users chosen here, who are not admins, can open this one too: from its sidebar entry, the Local Web UIs list or a dashboard card. They use it with the login or token stored here, and if it is trusted, its pages can act as them in Home Assistant. Sidebar entries are the same for everyone, so other users see this one's entry too, but cannot open it.
data_description.show_in_sidebar: Add a sidebar entry that opens this web UI directly.

discovery_confirm.title: Web UI of {name}
discovery_confirm.description: Open the web UI of {name} ({url}) inside Home Assistant? {subtitle}

error.invalid_url: Enter an http:// or https:// URL with a host.
error.invalid_token_header: Enter a header name made of letters, digits and dashes, other than one the proxy sets itself (such as Host, Cookie or Origin).
error.token_conflicts_with_login: The username is already sent in the Authorization header: send the token in another header, or leave the username empty.
error.invalid_identity_header: Enter a header name made of letters, digits and dashes, other than one the proxy sets itself (such as Host, Cookie or Origin).
error.identity_conflicts_with_authorization: The Authorization header already carries the username or the token: send who is viewing in another header.
error.identity_conflicts_with_token: The token is already sent in this header: choose another one.
error.invalid_audience: The audience is one word without spaces, usually the site's address.

abort.already_configured: This web UI is already set up.
abort.already_in_progress: This is already being set up.

hub.title: Local Web UIs options
hub.description: Options for all web UIs. Each web UI has settings of its own: the gear of its entry. The list of web UIs is at [Local Web UIs]({panel_url}). Web UIs that are told who is viewing get tokens from the issuer {issuer}.

data.show_panel: Show the list of web UIs in the sidebar
data.identity_url: Home Assistant's address for identity checks

data_description.discovery: Offer devices whose integration links to a local web page (their "Visit" button), such as ESPHome devices with web_server, WLED or printers. They appear under Discovered, where you add or ignore each.
data_description.link_device_pages: The default for each web UI of a device: point the device's own "Visit" button at its web UI here, so it also works away from home. Each web UI can choose otherwise in its settings. Turning it off restores the original links.
data_description.show_panel: The web UIs' own pages keep working when the list is hidden.
data_description.panel_icon: Icon of the list in the sidebar.
data_description.local_domains: Domains of your home network whose devices can be discovered, besides .local and .home.arpa, separated with spaces or commas (for example lan).{own_domain}
data_description.identity_url: Where the sites (or their gateway) reach Home Assistant to fetch the keys that check who is viewing; the issuer is this address followed by /api/local_web_ui/identity. Leave empty for Home Assistant's own address ({default_url}).
data_description.identity_claims:
Optional details added to the tokens of each person, by Home Assistant username (or user id). Tokens always carry the user id (sub), name and username (preferred_username); this can set another username, an email or groups, for example:
irena:
  preferred_username: irena
  email: irena@example.com
  groups: [family]
